findings.title: Required migration gates are absent from fast checks
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-43, RUST-01, RUST-02 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: pnpm check runs metadata, tsc and copies only. oxlint/oxlint-tsgolint and verify-code-rules are absent. Clippy/rustfmt are not wired for the five crates. Four crates lack the required lints table; the synced SSKR crate has it. The two cloud shell scripts do not start with set -euo pipefail; cloud-setup documents end-of-run error aggregation, which needs an explicit justified header exception rather than a blind -e addition.
findings.impact: Legacy violations remain invisible to the current green fast gate.
findings.recommendedFix: Introduce pinned type-aware lint and code-rules with negative controls; bring their actual scope green together. Add all-crate clippy/rustfmt and deliberate generated/data exclusions. Preserve the cloud script's intended error aggregation or redesign it coherently.
findings.requiredVerification: Gate controls refuse intentional violations; all repository fast gates pass. Rust source changes require separately authorized canonical WASM regeneration.

findings.title: Twenty-two action references differ from the approved pin table
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-10, CI-01 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: The local shared action-pins checker exits 1 with 22 mismatches for setup-node, upload-artifact and download-artifact.
findings.impact: Repository workflows have drifted from the workspace's single approved table; the references are still full hashes, so this does not demonstrate a mutable-tag vulnerability.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the already approved table consistently in this repository, without dispatching Actions.
findings.requiredVerification: Run node ../.github/scripts/verify-action-pins.mjs . and confirm zero differences.

findings.title: Large controllers and files remain outside the size and module migration
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-01, CORE-02, CORE-03, CORE-05, CORE-15, WEB-02 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: There are 17 physical files above 800 lines: 11 production, five tests, one tooling. No first-line size waiver is present. controller.ts is 1293 lines; createKeyDerivationController spans 1222 lines, its nested start spans 1214; Discovery view is 1143 lines and its factory spans 1023. There are 99 function spans above 150 (48 production, 45 test, six tooling), including nested wrappers and describe callbacks. These spans are candidates, not 99 independent oxlint failures. Five CSS files, two HTML templates and one consensus wordlist are included in the 17; data can require a named exclusion or justified exception rather than artificial splitting.
findings.impact: State, event handling, rendering and feature composition remain coupled, making the remaining migration substantially larger than a few renames.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate cohesive state/operation owners and keep thin installers. Split tests by behavior. Review long cohesive functions and data honestly; preserve template composition and consensus wordlist bytes.
findings.requiredVerification: Pinned size/lint gates, targeted behavior and secret-lifecycle tests, affected edition/selective compilation, and corresponding browser regression cases.

findings.title: Non-null assertions and compile-time private members remain
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow TS-03, TS-05 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: The AST inventory finds 288 non-null assertions in 89 production files and ten private fields/methods/parameter properties. Another eight private keywords restrict constructors; those are recorded separately and must not be blindly converted into impossible #constructors. Six any type nodes remain in tests, none in the owned production/tooling inventory. Test non-null assertions are allowed by TS-03 and are not findings.
findings.impact: The announced strict-code migration is incomplete. No actual missing-value runtime failure is established by the count alone.
findings.recommendedFix: Narrow/check values through their existing owning rule and replace private storage/methods with runtime private members. Resolve the constructor restriction explicitly in gate policy without broad suppressions. Remove test any types with real boundary fakes.
findings.requiredVerification: Type-aware lint with unused-exception reporting, typecheck and focused invariant/negative tests; preserve deterministic wallet outputs.

findings.title: Main and child wallets maintain the same display policy separately
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-10, CORE-14 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: BASIC_WINDOW_SIZE=200 and ADVANCED_WINDOW_SIZE=24 are independently declared and used for the same basic/advanced result window in controller.ts:38-39 and bip85-child-wallet-feature.ts:29,35. CHILD_WALLET_ID_PREFIX is also independently declared in the child feature and profile-template. There is no adjacent deliberate-copy justification. The copies gate passes because it detects long token runs, not semantic duplicate constants.
findings.impact: The two wallet displays or composed IDs can drift when only one declaration changes.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the shared display/markup contract one owner imported by host and build tooling where possible; preserve separate limits such as CHILD_RESULTS_LIMIT, whose meaning is different even when its value is also 200.
findings.requiredVerification: Test both result-window modes and composed child IDs against the shared owner; run composition and copies checks.

findings.title: An expected password-review wait is thrown as an error
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-22, TS-06 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: AwaitingAnswer extends Error (task.ts:12). PasswordReview.choose already returns a wait outcome, but require throws AwaitingAnswer at fields.ts:177; task and wallet flow catch it as ordinary expected control flow.
findings.impact: Expected UI progression is mixed with failures, contrary to CORE-22. Existing handlers distinguish it, so no false wallet verdict is alleged.
findings.recommendedFix: Carry a typed waiting outcome through the host operation result and reserve thrown errors for refusals. Preserve the upstream MHFE API and pending review ownership.
findings.requiredVerification: Password review wait/answer/edit/cancel tests; hidden-wallet session remains usable while waiting and failed operations remain failures.

findings.title: Host errors still rely on names and text instead of stable module codes
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-23, TS-06 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: Eight directly Error-derived classes in the inventory declare no code member. AwaitingAnswer, TextFileRefused and InvalidBuildSelection also lack the required Error suffix. There are 979 new Error/TypeError/RangeError constructions in owned production code and 434 in tooling: review inventory, not a count of independently confirmed defects. ProviderHttpError.status and PrivateMaterialError.name are not a module code. Imported MnemoCode/MHFE error catalogs are excluded and must not be hand-edited.
findings.impact: Callers remain coupled to exception classes/text and worker responses discard stable identity; migration is incomplete without demonstrating a new exploit.
findings.recommendedFix: Add owning module error identities, retain causes safely and build each frontend's text from codes. Keep refusals separate from expected results. Reuse existing error catalogs where they belong rather than creating a universal core error dependency.
findings.requiredVerification: Exact stable-code and refusal controls through real module/worker boundaries, safe diagnostics and existing cleanup/cancellation regressions.

findings.title: Many library export declarations lack public API contracts
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks an unqualified coding-guide compliance claim; no runtime compromise or release integrity failure is demonstrated by this finding alone.
findings.reproduction: Run the retained inventory and inspect the named source locations against the pinned coding guide.
findings.expected: Follow CORE-20, TS-11 within the guide's touched-code and gate-introduction applicability rules.
findings.observed: 413 of 684 top-level exported declarations under owned packages/*/src lack a leading JSDoc block in the syntax inventory. This counts declarations, not API members; re-export declarations and class members are not included. Even a present block still needs manual review for contract/errors/units. Examples include deriveBitcoin and the legacy derivation entry.
findings.impact: Public callers lack the contracts that the new guide requires; a mechanical comment count alone would overstate completion.
findings.recommendedFix: Document actual contracts, units, ownership and refusals alongside the owner/module refactoring; reduce unnecessary exports rather than adding meaningless comments.
findings.requiredVerification: Code-rules rejects an undocumented public declaration; review representative contracts against actual callers/tests and keep typecheck green.

limitations: Scoped CORE migration baseline, not a new whole-wallet security, protocol or release audit. Static inventory covers all enumerated owned source files; semantic reading is targeted, not line-by-line proof for all 968 files.

Imported MnemoCode source, generated WASM/MHFE, notices, fixtures, dependency internals, prior audit harnesses/evidence and ignored outputs are excluded from the owned-code counts. Their producer owns their migration. No sibling repository was edited.

No runtime wallet tests, full suite, vector replay, browser suite, Clippy execution, canonical build or release acceptance was performed for this baseline. Earlier results are historical only and are not added to these counts.

Existing examples of owner classes, ErrorCatalog use, strict compiler flags and single-source SSKR policy are retained progress; the migration is partial, not absent. Zero enum nodes and zero production any nodes are positive inventory observations, not full conformance proofs.

Review-only rules added later apply to touched code without a mandatory legacy sweep. A gate introduction covers its whole declared repository scope. The remaining plan must preserve this distinction and avoid unnecessary rewrites or speculative classes.

Function spans include nested functions, blanks/comments and describe wrappers. Public export comments require semantic review. No count is a vulnerability count. Eight private constructor restrictions are not private field violations.
No production, dependency, fixture, workflow or generated file was changed during this baseline. Only this report, its index entry and audit harnesses/evidence were added.

estimate.sequencing: The private migration handover requires the current dirty work to be committed before broad restructuring. No commit is authorized here. Finish and review the coherent integration changes, then obtain an explicit commit instruction before starting the separate migration tranche. Do not mix current integration with a wholesale rewrite.
